rules.title: Synthesised symbols are module-qualified by owning package
rules.statement: A symbol synthesised from a type/method belonging to package `pkg` is mangled as `<module_id>.<pkg>` when `pkg` belongs to a non-global module, and as `pkg` unchanged otherwise. This definition-side mangle is identical to the one applied at call sites, so a method-call symbol resolves to the emitted definition.

rules.title: Same-named structs from distinct packages are monomorphized independently
rules.statement: A concrete struct instance is keyed by `pkg.bare` when the type carries a package name, else by `bare`. Two structs with the same bare name from different packages (e.g. user `Box<i64>` vs `std.mem.box.Box<i64>`) receive distinct keys and are both instantiated in one compilation.

rules.title: Bare-name template fallback must not cross package boundaries
rules.statement: When resolving a package-qualified name `pkg.base` to a generic template, a bare-name `base` fallback is accepted only if the matched template's owning package equals `pkg`. A package-qualified non-generic struct never resolves to a same-named generic struct in a different package.

rules.title: Pointer to a custom-DST struct canonicalizes to a fat DstRef
rules.statement: A pointer `*mut S`/`*const S` to a struct `S` carrying an unsized (`[u8]`/slice) tail field is canonicalized to a fat DstRef representation, for non-generic as well as generic `S`; it is not left as a thin pointer.

rules.title: Best-matching partial specialization is selected over the generic base
rules.statement: Resolving a concrete struct type to its definition prefers the best-matching partial specialization (positionally), falling back to the generic base template (with positional type-var binding) only when no specialization matches. Layout/size computations use the definition that is actually emitted.

rules.title: Compile-time-constant call arguments specialize the callee
rules.statement: When a call-site argument forwarding (directly or transitively) to a const-evaluating intrinsic position (e.g. an atomic `Ordering`) is a compile-time literal, the callee is specialized with that constant baked in: each use of the parameter is replaced by the literal (an IntLit for integers, or an EnumLit `(enum_name, variant, discriminant)` for enums).
rules.divergence: Logos const-generic-like specialization driven by const-eval reachability; see explicit-metacall comptime model.

rules.title: Blanket impls are instantiated only for actually `dyn`-coerced targets
rules.statement: A blanket impl is not eagerly instantiated for all candidate types; for primitive and generic-struct-instantiation targets, the blanket is cloned only for types that are actually coerced to `dyn Trait` somewhere in the program (collected from `as dyn` casts).
rules.uncertainty: Restriction motivated by verification soundness (integer-bodied blanket fails on f32/f64); rule states the observable instantiation set.

rules.title: Generic struct methods are instantiated lazily, modulo pinned roots
rules.statement: Struct/enum methods of a generic type are instantiated on demand from call sites rather than eagerly per instantiation; methods that are trait-dispatch entries or explicitly root-pinned are force-instantiated even with no referencing call site.

rules.title: Entry points prune non-generic free functions to the reachable closure
rules.statement: When a non-empty entry-point set is supplied, only non-generic free functions transitively reachable (callee-discovery) from those entry points are monomorphized; with an empty set, all non-generic free functions are emitted.
